Thanks for the report. That sounds like a pretty critical issue. CC @godotengine/macos @godotengine/import 

It could be useful to narrow down which dev snapshot of 4.4 introduced the bug, which might give a hint as to which PR caused the problem. You could test intermediate 4.4 dev/beta/RC snapshots from https://godotengine.org/download/archive/ and see which is the first one to break / last one to work.
(I understand of course if you don't want to do testing that subjects your computer repeatedly to kernel panics.)
I can't reproduce it on M4 Mac. Both reports seem to be from M2, so it might be hardware specific.

BTW @Wharenn @p-7 did you experience this in previous weeks, or did the issue start recently? I noticed you both reported this the same day, while 4.4 has been released for nearly 3 months, so I wonder if it's a system update that triggered the bug, or if it's just a coincidence that you both decided to report it now.
I have an M2 Pro that is still on Sonoma 14.6.1, so I can test and confirm if older versions are okay
For the reference, I was testing on 15.5 (24F74). Also tested on M1 with 15.4 installed, and was not able t reproduce it either. I'll update it to 15.5 and recheck when it's done.

@akien-mga the issue also happened with Sequoia 15.4.1. I updated yesterday to see if it fixed the issue, with no luck.

I can't really tell when it really started. I would saw a few weeks ago. At the beginning, I thought it was due to my project using more and more 3d assets and some assets being buggy (this is my first project in 3D).
I can't reproduce with Godot v4.4.1.stable - macOS Sonoma (14.6.1) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Metal (Forward+) - integrated Apple M2 (Apple8) - Apple M2 (8 threads)
Was not able to reproduce on M1 with 15.5 either.

> BTW [@Wharenn](https://github.com/Wharenn) [@p-7](https://github.com/p-7) did you experience this in previous weeks, or did the issue start recently? I noticed you both reported this the same day, while 4.4 has been released for nearly 3 months, so I wonder if it's a system update that triggered the bug, or if it's just a coincidence that you both decided to report it now.

(I understand of course if you don't want to do testing that subjects your computer repeatedly to kernel panics.)

I tested the 4.4.0 dev snapshots and found the first issue of this bug on 4.4.0-dev2 snapshot. 4.4.0-dev1 is fine.

~~Sadly, I am forced to rollback my project to 4.3 as I am no more able to load it without making my Macbook to reboot~~
(found workaround [below](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/106801#issuecomment-2916163533))

I’m back with more info which I hope will help narrow down the underlying issue. It seems the issue, on my side, is somehow related to screen resolution and possibly the Godot window width on the screen. I’m working with an external 4K screen (Gigabyte M28U for the record). I found out that only one resolution on this screen (3360x1890) triggers the issue, others do not, even higher ones. Here are all the resolutions available for this screen: When using the MacBook’s internal display, none of its resolutions cause issues (though 3360x1890 isn’t available). When using dual screens (MacBook open + 4K external), the issue only appears when the Godot window is on the 4K screen, not when it’s on the MacBook display. This led me to investigate a correlation between the issue and the Godot window size. I noticed that below a certain width, the issue doesn’t appear. The black jittering grows progressively as the editor window increases in width. This setup doesn’t cause jittering (and I couldn’t reproduce a crash through spam reimport): This setup starts showing jittering (~20% screen height): This setup causes massive jittering (~80% screen height): To reiterate: the jittering only happens at 3360x1890, not at 3840x2160, so it’s not just a matter of window size. Screenshots do not show any jittering as it is not recordable, but it does appear. Apologies if I’ve shared too much detail. Since the issue isn’t reproducible on all M2 setups, I explored every lead I could to give the most useful insights. As a workaround, switching my external screen to a different resolution prevents the issue. @p-7 could you check whether these findings/setup match your own?

> I found out that only one resolution on this screen (3360x1890) triggers the issue, others do not, even higher ones.

I have retested in with the same resolution on M4, but still can't reproduce it.
@stuartcarnie Any chance you have an external screen and can test and repro this issue?
I have an external 4K monitor, but I don't have an M2. I'll try and see if I can duplicate the issue.

> [@stuartcarnie](https://github.com/stuartcarnie) Any chance you have an external screen and can test and repro this issue?

I tried multiple times, reimporting and could not reproduce using the MRP

I tried opening the MRP and spamming re-import on my second monitor, did not manage to reproduce the issue (M1 Max, Sequoia 15.3).

Note that Sequoia 15.6 is now available. Might be worth trying if it fixes the issue [@Wharenn](https://github.com/Wharenn) [@p-7](https://github.com/p-7).
@stuartcarnie @Ivorforce To clarify, you tested with a 3360x1890 resolution?
No, just some regular resolution. I figured the chances were slim with previous tests but i wanted to try anyway.

@Ivorforce the OP was only ever able to repro when using 3360x1890 resolution. So tests at other resolutions shouldn't show the bug in any case

See above https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/106801#issuecomment-2916163533

> [@stuartcarnie](https://github.com/stuartcarnie) [@Ivorforce](https://github.com/Ivorforce) To clarify, you tested with a 3360x1890 resolution?

Alright then, thanks for testing. Downgrading from a release blocker since none of us can reproduce the issue

@Wharenn thanks for the report, it seems that you are running into a similar hardware issue to [this comment](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/106106#issuecomment-3037182314) for issue #106106. Also notice in your report that the panic occurred in a browser renderer and not Godot:

```
Panicked task 0xfffffe199ba60e38: 16184 pages, 20 threads: pid 48055: Browser Helper (Renderer)
```

Their hardware was also an M2, which still may be coincidental, but certainly notable. It could be that under these conditions, Godot is putting the right amount of stress on memory to trigger an issue.

After some additional research, I have found that this problem has been raised elsewhere. This is not a Godot-specific issue, and unfortunately, none of the Godot maintainers have been able to reproduce the issue.

Both of these issues indicate display configuration issues may trigger the error:

- https://github.com/Genymobile/scrcpy/issues/5072
- https://github.com/waydabber/BetterDisplay/discussions/2981
